newsitem.title: UK: Britain should vaccinate all children against hepatitis - experts.
newsitem.headline: Britain should vaccinate all children against hepatitis - experts.

text.p: Medical experts urged British authorities on Friday to vaccinate all youngsters against Hepatitis B, the potentially fatal liver disease that is 100 times more infectious than AIDS.

Professor Arie Zuckerman, chairman of the medical panel calling for universal vaccination of children, said: "Hepatitis B is a very serious, yet preventable disease, which currently kills one to two million people every year worldwide."
Seventy-five countries have already introduced universal vaccination for Hepatitis B and Zuckerman urged Britain to follow suit, saying that 25 percent of cases among children proved fatal.

"Over the past 10 years there have been major demographic changes within the UK and an increase in foreign travel. This means that more UK individuals are at risk of contracting hepatitis B," he told reporters.
But a spokesman for the department of health insisted that Britain had one of the lowest rates in the world.

"The Government's position is that we advise immunisation for people who are considered to be at increased risk. We are looking into the WHO proposals for universal childhood vaccination but it is still under review," he added.
